Then, (a3 - b3)/(a2 + ab + b2)

= (a - b)(a2 + ab + b2)/(a2 + ab + b2)

= 2 + 3√2 - 3 + 2√2

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statement is true?

I. 167+116 is odd

II. 155-124 is even
questions.solution_en:
I. 167+116

When an even number is multiplied by another even number then their solution will be even. So,

167will be even.

Similarly, when an odd number is multiplied by another odd number then their solution will be odd. So, 116 will be odd.

Sum of an even number and an odd number always gives an odd value.

So, 167+116 is odd.

Hence, statement I is true.

II. 155-124

When an odd number is multiplied by another odd number then their solution will be odd. So,

155 will be odd.

Similarly, when an even number is multiplied by another even number then their solution will be even. So, 124will be even.

Difference between an even number and an odd number always gives an odd value.

So, 155-124 is odd.

Hence, statement II is wrong.

questions.q_en:
The following line graph shows the percentage increase in the number of employees in four departments - A, B, C and D from year 2002 to year 2003.

The number of employees in departments A and C in 2002 were in the ratio 2: 3 respectively and number of employees in department C in 2003 was 135 more than that in department A in 2003. Find the total number of employees in departments A and C together in 2002.
questions.solution_en:
Let number of employees in department A in 2002 = 2x

And number of employees in department C in 2002 = 3x

Number of employees in department A in 2003 = 2x + 2x * (20/100) = 12x/5

Number of employees in department C in 2003 = 3x + 3x * (25/100) = 15x/4

Given,

(15x/4) - (12x/5) = 135

(75x - 48x) = 135 * 20

27x = 135 * 20

x = 5 * 20 = 100

Total number of employees in departments A and C together in 2002 = 2x + 3x = 5x = 500

questions.q_en: If x is an odd number and y is an even number, then which of the following is an odd number?
questions.solution_en:
x = odd, so let x = 2n + 1, where n is any positive integer

y = even, so let y = 2m, where m is any positive integer

x + y + 1 = 2n + 1 + 2m + 1 = 2n + 2m + 2 = 2(n + m + 1), which is even

xy = (2n + 1)2m = 2m(2n + 1), which is even

xy + y = 2m(2n + 1) + 2m = 2m(2n + 2), which is even

x + y + 2 = 2n + 1 + 2m + 2 = 2n + 2m + 3 = 2(n + m + 1) + 1, so it is odd.

A dishonest fruit-seller sells fruits at 20% profit but he uses 950 gm weight in place of 1 kg. What is the profit per cent?
questions.solution_en:
Let the Cost Price of 1 kg fruits be ₹100.

Selling Price of 1 kg fruits = ₹100 + 20% of ₹100

=> ₹100 + ₹20 = ₹120

He uses 950 gm instead of 1 kg.

Therefore, Selling Price of 950 gm fruits = ₹120

Now, Cost Price of 950 gm fruits = 950/1000 X 100 = ₹95

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

=> ₹120 - ₹95 = ₹25

Profit % = 25/95 * 100 = (500/19)%
